newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: MORE PRIVATISATION NEEDED, EU COMMISSION SAYS.
newsitem.headline: MORE PRIVATISATION NEEDED, EU COMMISSION SAYS.

text.p: The European Commission said in its report on Lithuania on Wednesday that it needed to boost privatisation and improve bankruptcy proceedings but said recent improvements in policy would accelerate the market economy.

The Commission made the remarks in its report on the various eastern European nations that have applied to be EU members. The Commission has recommended that talks begin with five eastern Europeans, including Estonia.
"Lithuania would face serious difficulties to cope with competitive pressure and market forces within the Union in the medium term," the Commission said in its report.
"The marked recent improvement in policy would, if sustained, accelerate the establishment of a market economy and strengthen competitiveness," it added.
But it said that restructuring of enterprises needed to be carried out, agriculture needed to be modernised and that the bank sector was still weak.

"...futher progress is needed, particularly in the areas of relative price adjustments, large-scale privatisation and bankruptcy proceedings. The main element still missing is the enforcement of financial discipline for enterprises," it said.

On the positive side, the Commission said that industry should be able to cope with integration into the single market in the medium term and it did not have difficulties in fields including education, trade and international economic relations.
The Commission stressed that the government must agree to the timetable to shut the Ignalina power station and upgrade safety standards to international levels.
But it saw no other problems in the energy sector apart from work on monopolies, access to networks and energy pricing.
